- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.23 or higher) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.11 or lower) — model shows mean-reversion bias, underreacting to bearish signals.
- Lag in downward corrections: model often delays price drops, especially after strong negative sentiment, leading to overestimation of future lows.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment volatility — model amplifies sentiment-driven swings, especially in 30-day horizon, leading to overfitting to recent sentiment.
- Mean-reversion bias in mid-range price zones — model tends to overcorrect upward from recent lows, then undercorrect downward from recent highs.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating upward momentum when sentiment is bullish, and underestimating downward momentum when sentiment is bearish.
